title: File an FIR, e-FIR or Zero FIR
summary: Report a cognizable offence to police.
steps: Go to any police station (Zero FIR) or use your state police's citizen portal for e-FIR where available.
Give a clear written account: date, time, place, persons involved, witnesses.
For an e-FIR, visit the police station to sign it within 3 days.
Collect your free FIR copy and note the FIR number.
If police refuse, send the complaint in writing/post to the Superintendent of Police; next, approach the Judicial Magistrate.
jurisdiction: India (Central); state portals and practice vary

title: If you or someone is detained / arrested
summary: Immediate steps to protect your rights.
steps: Stay calm. Ask for the grounds of arrest and the officer's identity.
Ask police to inform a family member or friend of the arrest and place of detention.
Ask to meet an advocate. If you cannot afford one, ask for free legal aid (NALSA 15100).
Do not sign blank papers. You need not confess — confessions to police are not admissible.
Ensure production before a magistrate within 24 hours.
Ask for a medical examination if injured.
Contact an advocate immediately about bail.
jurisdiction: India (Central); state portals and practice vary

title: File a consumer complaint
summary: Complain about defective goods or poor service.
steps: Send a written complaint/legal notice to the seller or service provider and keep proof.
Call the National Consumer Helpline 1915 for mediation.
Gather bills, warranty, communication and photos.
File online on e-Daakhil with the District Commission (pecuniary limits apply).
Pay the prescribed fee and attend hearings online or in person.
jurisdiction: India (Central); state portals and practice vary

title: Report cyber / UPI fraud
steps: Immediately call 1930 (Cyber Fraud Helpline).
Inform your bank to block the card/account.
Register a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in with transaction details.
Keep screenshots, SMS, call logs and URLs.
Follow up with the local cyber cell using your acknowledgement number.
jurisdiction: India (Central); state portals and practice vary

title: File an RTI application
summary: Request information from a public authority.
steps: Identify the public authority holding the information.
Write the application under Section 6(1) with specific questions.
Pay the fee (₹10 for central government; state fees vary; BPL applicants exempt).
For central ministries, file online at rtionline.gov.in.
If no reply in 30 days, file a first appeal under Section 19.
jurisdiction: India (Central); state portals and practice vary

title: Get protection from domestic violence
steps: In danger, call 112 or Women Helpline 181.
Contact the Protection Officer or a registered service provider in your district.
A Domestic Incident Report can be prepared.
Apply to the Magistrate under Section 12 of the PWDVA for protection/residence/monetary orders.
Free legal aid is available from the District Legal Services Authority.
jurisdiction: India (Central); state portals and practice vary

title: Pay or contest a traffic challan
steps: Check the challan on the e-Challan portal using vehicle or challan number.
Pay online if correct.
If wrong, raise a grievance on the portal or contest at the virtual/traffic court.
Keep evidence (photos, location data) to support your case.
jurisdiction: India (Central); state portals and practice vary
